newsitem.title: UK: Fannie Mae says demand drove stg bond increase.
newsitem.headline: Fannie Mae says demand drove stg bond increase.

text.p: U.S. home loans group Fannie Mae increased its debut sterling global bond to 1.25 billion stg due to continued demand for the issue, its treasurer Linda Knight told Reuters in a telephone interview on Wednesday.
"We increased the issue because from the very beginning we found that the deal was well oversubscribed," Knight said.
Fannie Mae priced a 1.0 billion stg June 2002 global bond on February 12 via joint lead managers BZW and Merrill Lynch.
The bond yielded 10 basis points over the 7.0 percent gilt due June 2002. Today's increase of 250 million stg was priced to yield eight b.p. over the gilt.
"Since then we have continued to see interest in the deal in the secondary market and because of the depth of interest it was appropriate to reopen it," Knight said.
"We now have a larger more liquid deal which is very invaluable to investors," she said.
She said there was very good demand from Asia and Europe for the increase.
The original issue saw a sales distribution of 48 percent into Britain, 19 percent into Asia, 20 percent into Continental Europe and 13 percent into the U.S.
